name: Workshop Null  Kairos Synestherion Mk.II
description:
The Kairos Synestherion Mk.II is the second and final iteration produced by Workshop Null, a three-person artisan collective operating from an undisclosed fabrication space within GLMZ's industrial mid-ring. Produced in a run of exactly 22 units — the collective has publicly stated no further production is planned — the Synestherion is a radical synesthetic BCI that permanently and deliberately reconfigures the cross-modal mapping of the wearer's sensory cortex. Rather than simulating synesthesia as an overlay, the Kairos rewires the underlying architecture: sound genuinely activates visual processing, emotional states manifest as tactile sensation across the skin, mathematical relationships produce olfactory signatures, and social dynamics are perceived as harmonic chord structures. The implant uses a hybrid of photonic signal routing and biochemical neuromodulator micro-infusion to achieve stable, persistent cross-modal binding, with a real-time adaptive algorithm that continuously refines the synesthetic mappings based on the user's neurological feedback over the first 90 days post-installation — a process Workshop Null calls 'blooming.'

Within artistic communities across GLMZ, the Synestherion has achieved something approaching mythological status. The 22 known Kairos users — who call themselves, without apparent irony, the 'Bloom' — produce work that defies conventional categorization: compositions that are simultaneously music and architecture, paintings that are also mathematical proofs experienced as scent-landscapes. Three Bloom members have held solo exhibitions at the Meridian Cultural Nexus; one, the sculptor-composer known only as Vessel, was offered TESSERA's artist residency stipend and publicly declined. Critics argue the Kairos represents the most significant development in human aesthetic perception since the invention of the electromagnetic spectrum display. Others argue that permanently altering one's neurology for art is a form of self-destruction Workshop Null is ethically obligated to prevent. Workshop Null has not responded.
tier_availability: Tier 5 — Exotic/Artisan. 22 units produced total across Mk.I and Mk.II. No waitlist; collective states production is permanently closed.
legality: Restricted — Class III Neurological Modification. Permanent cortical reconfiguration requires Meridian Medical Authority sign-off. Several units were installed without authorization; legal status of those installations is contested.
installation_requirements: Workshop Null installs personally — no third-party installation available or supported. Pre-installation neurological mapping session (6 hours). Installation requires 11-hour procedure. Mandatory 90-day 'blooming' monitoring period with weekly collective check-ins.
rejection_risk: Low-Moderate (8%) — primarily during blooming period. Post-bloom rejection risk drops to <1%. Mk.II improved significantly on Mk.I's 19% blooming-phase rejection rate.
maintenance: Annual recalibration by Workshop Null only (fee negotiated individually). Proprietary neuromodulator refill every 6 months (Φ8,000–Φ15,000 depending on supply). No remote diagnostics — physical attendance required.

side_effects: Permanent alteration of baseline sensory experience — synesthetic perception does not switch off; users describe it as learning to live in a 'richer but sometimes overwhelming' world
Significant adjustment period (3–6 months post-bloom) during which overstimulation in complex sensory environments (crowds, loud spaces, emotionally charged situations) can cause acute disorientation
Mathematical or linguistic input (reading, calculation) produces persistent olfactory sensations that some users find intrusive in professional contexts
Deep emotional states — grief, ecstasy, rage — manifest as full-body tactile experiences that can be physically incapacitating at peak intensity
cultural_context: The 'Bloom' — the 22 Kairos users — have become a cultural phenomenon within GLMZ's artistic underground. They share a perceptual world that is, in a very literal neurological sense, inaccessible to anyone else, and their art reflects this: beautiful, disorienting, and frequently accused of being 'untranslatable.' Some cultural theorists argue the Bloom represents the first post-human artistic movement, created by minds that have been deliberately made different. Workshop Null maintains a strict policy of silence on the subject, issuing no statements, giving no interviews, and communicating with the outside world only through the art of their clients.
known_users: Vessel — sculptor-composer, identity undisclosed beyond art name
Dr. Fen Cassiday — former Meridian Medical Authority neurologist, resigned to pursue full-time artistic practice post-installation
The individual known as 'Seventh Bloom' — only Kairos user known to have sought partial reversal; current status unknown
story_hooks: A 23rd Kairos Synestherion has appeared — Workshop Null denies producing it, and its synesthetic mappings are subtly, disturbingly wrong in ways that the Bloom describe as 'feeling like a voice speaking in your language but meaning something else entirely.'

One of the Bloom has gone missing, and the art they left behind — a 40-hour installation piece — appears to contain, encoded in its synesthetic cross-modal structure, a detailed record of what they witnessed before they disappeared.

Workshop Null has contacted a fixer with an unusual offer: locate a specific individual who stole the Mk.I prototype schematics before the Mk.II was designed, in exchange for consideration for one of three Synestherion units the collective claims to have secretly held in reserve.
